title: Abhivādana: the formal greeting

words.meaning: I salute, I announce myself in greeting

words.gram: compound stem, in a compound with the following gotra
words.meaning: endowed with the pravara (the line of ancestral seers)

translation.literal: I salute: (I am) of the gotra (…), endowed with the pravara of three seers (…), of the (Āpastamba) sūtra, a student of the Yajus branch; (…) Śarmā by name I am, O sirs!
translation.readable: I greet you: I am …, of the … gotra, with a pravara of three seers …, following the Āpastamba sūtra, a student of the Yajurveda — … Śarmā by name.

meaning: The abhivādana is the formal greeting in which one announces oneself by lineage: the seers of one’s pravara, the gotra, the sūtra of one’s rites, the Veda one studies, and one’s name. S prints it as a formula with blanks: the parentheses and the empty brackets mark the places where each performer puts his own seers, gotra and name (M fills them with a worked example for the Bhāradvāja gotra). The words in parentheses — trayārṣeya, āpastamba — are the common case and are replaced when they do not apply (pañcārṣeya for five seers, another sūtra or Veda).
in_the_rite: Said with a bow, touching the ears, after kāmo ’kārṣīt (step samasti-abhivadana) and again at the end of the salutation to Sūrya-Nārāyaṇa, in all three services.

flags.text: S writes the formula with pausal forms around its blanks (गोत्रः (आपस्तम्ब), सूत्रः यजुः-): the visarga is kept before a vowel and before y. The engine accepts a kept visarga only before a vowel (declared); सूत्रः यजुःशाखा does not rejoin. The record cannot be proven until the checker treats a blank as a pause or the text is joined.
